Bill.BriefDescription: Reducing the number of employees in Washington management service.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to reducing the number of employees in theWashington management service; adding new sections to chapter 41.06RCW; and creating a new section.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The legislature finds that excessive growthin state spending and ongoing expenditure obligations have created abudget crisis of critical proportions which requires immediate anddemanding fiscal discipline. Serious and comprehensive measures mustbe taken to reduce the costs of government as quickly as possible andto ensure that citizens are not burdened with even higher taxes.Reassessing the function and control of the Washington managementservice is an essential part of resolving this budget crisis. The legislature further finds that organizations with larger staffper manager ratios are more efficient, and that state government canbecome more effective and less costly by reducing the layers ofmanagement, enlarging each manager's span of control, focusingdecisionmaking authority, and moving decisionmaking authority downinto units which provide services directly to the citizens. This willallow faster, more peopleoriented decision making, lower management p. 1 HB 1132costs, improve employee satisfaction and motivation, create moreopportunities for development of employee skills, put greatermanagement focus on planning and goals, reduce duplication of tasks,roles, and responsibilities, ensure less micromanagement, speeddecision making, provide clearer communication between bottom and toplayers, make for less paperwork due to fewer reporting requirements,decrease the need for managementsupport staff, and result in fewerplanning and coordination meetings.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 41.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: No agency may employ personnel who are classified as managers withsupervisory job titles but who have no direct subordinates.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 41.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Unless prohibited by federal law, each agency shall have no morethan one manager with a supervisory job title for each twentyfivenonmanagement employees within the agency.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 41.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Each agency must reduce the number of employees in the Washingtonmanagement service by twentyfive percent no later than December 31,2003.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 41.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Any reductions in the number of Washington management serviceemployees within an agency shall not result in an increase ofclassified employees within the agency. Any reductions in the numberof Washington management service employees within the state shall notresult in an increase of classified employees within the state.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 41.06 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: Section 2, 3, or 4 of this act shall not apply if the governorcertifies to the legislature that substantive and compelling reasons HB 1132 p. 2 exist that an agency should be exempt from complying with theprovisions of this act. The governor shall submit findings andconclusions to support the certification based on empirical facts thatshow by clear and convincing evidence that the public will be harmed ifthe agency were to comply with the provisions of this act.
